finding.title: Fix learning_tracker/Makefile check 15/15 cross-feature-import awk — it can never detect a violation
finding.rule: Rule 0 (checker must actually fail) / Rule 2 (no cross-feature deep imports)

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

finding.why: grep -n emits 'path:line:content', so the file's own path (which always contains 'features/<owning-feature>/') appears in $0 BEFORE the import statement text. awk's match($0, /features\/([^/]+)\//, b) returns the FIRST match in the line — the file's own feature — not the imported feature, so b[1] always equals a[1] (both extracted from the same file-path segment) and the `a[1] != b[1]` guard can never be true. Reproduced directly: running the exact pipeline against lib/features/ yields 0 hits, and the committed baseline (docs/audits/standards-audit-2026-07-03/_work/baseline/make-audit.txt) shows check 15/15 printing no WARN block at all — a silent, false PASS. My batch alone contains ~50 real deep cross-feature import lines (dashboard/, scheduler/, sync/, onboarding/, content_browsing/, profiles/, settings/ providers imported directly instead of via a feature barrel) that this check should be listing as warn-only violations and never does.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to extract the imported feature name from the import token specifically (e.g. `grep -oP "features/[^/]+/" <<<"$import_part"` after splitting off the file:line prefix), verify it now emits the WARN list, then use it to start triaging the real cross-feature-import backlog per Rule 2.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic fixture file importing a different feature's deep path makes `make audit` check 15/15 print a WARN/file:line for it
Running the fixed check against current lib/features/tracks/setup/** surfaces its real deep cross-feature imports instead of zero
